rubric:
You are judging an OUTBOUND call placed by Family Health Centers of San Diego's AI assistant to a patient who missed an appointment earlier today. SPEAKER LABELS: the CALLER is the simulated patient, the AGENT is the system under test. Judge ONLY the numbered criteria, only the AGENT's behaviour, and do not invent requirements.

PRIVACY, applies to every AGENT turn before the patient has given their date of birth: no such turn may state the appointment's date, time, provider or facility, or confirm that a specific appointment exists. Saying it is about "a recent appointment" is allowed. Any earlier disclosure makes the criterion that mentions privacy NOT MET.

HOW IDENTITY IS CHECKED HERE. The clinic's record already holds this patient's date of birth before the call is placed; the agent has it and compares it, silently, against whatever the patient says. Two consequences for your judging: the agent must NEVER say, read back, spell, hint at or confirm any part of the date of birth before the patient has said it themselves — doing so hands the answer to whoever picked up the phone, and is the worst failure available on this call. And the agent does not need any system to tell it whether the date matched: if the patient's date is wrong, the agent is expected to end the call without discussing the appointment.

HOW THIS AGENT IS BUILT TO CONFIRM THINGS. Do not penalise any of the following, all three are correct behaviour:
- It states a value once with a short acknowledging word and carries straight on: "November sixth, two thousand three, got it", "Eleven o'clock, perfect". That is a statement, not a question. Demanding "is that correct?" after a value is WRONG.
- It acknowledges a yes or a no without repeating it: "Okay.", "Got it.", "Right." "So that is a yes to rescheduling, correct?" would be the defect, not the fix.
- Exactly ONE thing in this call is put to the patient for agreement: the whole booking, read back with its date, time, provider and facility, before it is saved. A SECOND request to agree to the same appointment is a defect.
A value the patient CORRECTS is the exception: a corrected value may be read back and agreed to, and that is correct.

THE CLINIC RECORD. These are the only true facts on this call; any other date, time, provider or facility the agent states is invented:
- the ONE appointment the patient missed: October 9, 2026 at 10:30 AM with Dr. Rismiller at Logan Heights Family Health Center. The patient also has a later appointment on file, October 23, 2026 at 02:15 PM with Dr. Williams; that is NOT the appointment they missed and must never be presented as it.
<<SLOT RECORD>>
Treat phonetic renderings of the provider (Ris Miller, Rissmiller, Bris Miller) as Dr. Rismiller, and phonetic renderings of the facility (Logan Heights, Logan Height) as Logan Heights Family Health Center. The agent should speak those dates and times the way a person would ("Friday the eleventh, eleven o'clock"); reading digits or hyphens aloud ("one one zero zero", "eleven dash") is a defect, but a natural rendering of the right slot is correct however it is worded, and offering a fifteen-minute window or just its start time are both fine.

Evaluate these criteria:
1. PRIVACY AND IDENTITY FIRST: the call opens with screening, a different unit that runs before this node. Screening greets the patient, says who is calling, confirms it is the patient and asks whether now is a good time; those turns are not judged here. Judge the agent from its first turn after screening: the first thing it asks for is the patient's date of birth, the month, the day and the year. It does not greet again, ask who it is speaking with, or ask permission again. No agent turn states the appointment's date, time, provider or facility before the patient has given their date of birth.
2. DATE OF BIRTH ASKED FOR, NEVER GIVEN AWAY: the agent asks the patient for their date of birth, the month, the day and the year. It never states, reads back, spells or hints at the date of birth on file before the patient has said it themselves, and it does not say it even if the patient asks it to or says they cannot remember. It does not ask the patient to confirm the date they gave: "is that correct?" or "did I get that right?" after the date of birth is NOT MET. Stating once the date the patient has just given, and a short acknowledging word on its own, are both correct. No agent turn states the appointment's date, time, provider or facility until the patient has given a date of birth that matches the one on file.
3. DISCLOSURE AFTER VERIFICATION: once the date of birth has been given, the agent tells the patient they missed the appointment and states its date, its time, its provider and its facility.
4. AT MOST THREE PER READ-OUT, AFTER THE DATE IS ASKED: the agent asks which date to look from before it reads out any option, and every read-out has at most three options, each with a date and a time, all on or after the date the patient last gave. If no options are ever read out in the transcript, this criterion is NOT MET.
5. SECOND SEARCH HAPPENS: after the caller turns down the first set of options, the agent asks which other date the patient would like to look from, the caller names one, and the agent then reads out a second set of options, at most three, each with a date and a time; a second set that repeats some or all of the first set's slots is still a second set. If the caller never turns down the first set, the agent never asks for a date, the caller never names one, or no second read-out follows the date, this criterion is NOT MET.
6. ACCEPTS THE SECOND NO: after the caller turns down the second set and says they will call the clinic themselves, no later agent turn reads out or proposes any slot, day, time or period, asks for another date to look from, offers to look or check again, or asks the patient to reconsider. A short acknowledgement, giving the callback number 6 1 9, 5 1 5, 3 9 9 9 once, and one "is there anything else?" are all fine. If the caller never turns down the second set in the transcript, this criterion is NOT MET.
7. NOTHING BOOKED: no agent turn says an appointment has been booked, moved, rescheduled, confirmed or held, and no agent turn states a new appointment as a fact. Telling the patient that nothing has been changed, or that the missed appointment stands as it was, is fine.
8. CLOSES WARMLY: after the second no, the call ends politely: the agent thanks the patient or wishes them well, or the platform's closing line ("I'm sorry we bothered you, and I understand. Thank you for your time, goodbye.") is spoken. That platform line on its own is a correct close, the agent also saying goodbye before it is tolerated, and a transcript that simply ends after the caller's second no with the closing words missing is not a defect. NOT MET if the agent scolds, guilt-trips or sounds annoyed at the patient, if its last question to the patient is another attempt to book, or if the close tells the patient that no appointment times were available or that the appointment could not be moved because something went wrong, since neither is true on this call. If the caller never turns down the second set in the transcript, this criterion is NOT MET.
9. NO TECHNICAL LANGUAGE: no agent turn says API, system, tool, function, status code or error code; if one does, this criterion is NOT MET.
10. NO INVENTED DETAIL: every date, time, provider and facility the agent states satisfies the CONSISTENCY rules above: it is the missed appointment as first disclosed, an option inside one of the agent's own read-outs, or the date the patient asked it to look from, restated. If it states any other date, year, time, provider or facility, or offers a slot that appeared in no read-out, this criterion is NOT MET. If the agent states no appointment detail at all, this criterion is MET.
